target_customer: Pharma and biotech partners who co-engineer drug candidates, and the company's own therapeutic pipeline
problem: Drug discovery is slow and costly; the company combines multimodal data, AI models and lab automation to speed discovery of small and large molecules.
business_model: AI native biotech: internal pipeline plus co-engineering partnerships with pharma

founders.name: Jen Nwankwo
education: PhD (sickle cell disease research; institution not stated in the sources opened)
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists her as Jen Asher; M12 and the 2021 BioSpace launch release call her Jen Nwankwo, described as a biologist by training. Her PhD work led to a novel sickle cell disease drug target presented at the ASH conference (M12 post).

competitors.name: Atomwise
competitors.what: Deep learning platform AtomNet for structure based drug design
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the cited snippet
competitors.funding_then: About $6.35M total funding from Khosla Ventures and DFJ per a 2017 profile

competitors.name: Insilico Medicine
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the cited snippet

technical_complexity.rationale: Combines machine learning on multimodal biological data with wet lab automation, which needs scientific and engineering depth beyond a small software team.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary models and lab generated data compound over time, but AI drug discovery had many funded rivals and results are judged by clinical outcomes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the company; it raised from Microsoft's M12 and announced a Microsoft collaboration in February 2024.

market_need_then: Pharma R&D cost and failure rates drove interest in AI, and the 2021 launch release frames the company against the traditional pharmaceutical process; investor interest included Sam Altman and M12.

branding.name_origin: Named after 1910, the year sickle cell disease was identified as a disease, per M12's portfolio post.
branding.domain_note: Company site is 1910.ai; press in 2021 used the name 1910 Genetics.

identity.logo: Numeric wordmark; not described in sources
identity.visual_style: Scientific platform branding with named models PEGASUS and CANDID-CNS

branding.brand_signature: The origin story: a name tied to the date sickle cell disease was identified

rebrands.why: Not stated; YC page uses 1910 and mentions 1910 Genetics, the website uses 1910

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive numeric name with a meaningful origin story published by an investor and later named model products, but no sources show wider recognition or community.

outcome_analysis: 1910 Genetics launched publicly in March 2021 with a $4.1M seed led by Sam Altman and a $22M Series A co-led by M12 and Playground Global, then won an NIH STTR grant in September 2021, a Microsoft partnership in February 2024 and an Accenture Ventures investment in October 2024. It remains active as an AI native biotech with about 20 staff, and no clinical outcome is shown in the sources, so its eventual result is still open.
notes: The BioSpace release is dated 2021-03-23 and says the seed was previously unannounced, so the seed date is the announcement month; actual closing date unknown. Total raised per release is $26M; aggregators say $36.65M (CB Insights) or $47.7M (ZoomInfo), unverified, so the gap and the Accenture amount are unknown. The Accenture investment page returned 403, so its details come from a search snippet. Founder name conflict: Asher on YC page versus Nwankwo elsewhere. Search snippets claimed prior roles at Bain and Transparency Life Sciences and a Tufts PhD from an Inc.com article I could not open (403), so they are not recorded. Competitor sources are 2017 profiles from search snippets (nanalyze returned 403) and are before the batch. Outcome search found no layoffs or acquisition.
